questions.question: On an analog clock the hour hand sits just past the 2, and the minute hand points straight at the 6. Remember: from one number to the next number is 5 minutes. What time is it?
questions.explain: The hour hand has passed the 2 but has not reached the 3, so the hour is 2. The minute hand on the 6 means 6 groups of 5 = 30 minutes, so it is 2:30. The common trap is reading the hour as the number ahead and saying 3:30 — the hour is always the number the hour hand has already gone past.

questions.question: On an analog clock the hour hand is between the 7 and the 8, and the minute hand points straight at the 9. Counting by 5s from the 12, what time does the clock show?
questions.explain: The hour hand is past 7 and not yet at 8, so the hour is 7; the minute hand on the 9 is 9 fives = 45 minutes, giving 7:45 (quarter to 8). The trap is jumping the hour hand up to the number in front of it and writing 8:45.

questions.question: On an analog clock face there are 12 numbers, and the minute hand moves 5 minutes to go from one number to the next. The minute hand starts at the 12 and travels all the way around the face once, back to the 12. How many minutes have gone by?
questions.explain: Skip-count by 5 for each of the 12 numbers: 12 groups of 5 = 60 minutes, and 60 minutes is exactly 1 hour, so the hour hand has moved to the next number. The trap is counting the 12 numbers instead of the minutes they stand for.

questions.question: On an analog clock the hour hand is a little past the 11, and the minute hand points straight at the 3. What time is it?
questions.explain: The hour hand has only just left the 11, so the hour is 11; the minute hand on the 3 means 3 fives = 15 minutes, so it is 11:15, or quarter past 11. The trap is reading the hour hand as the next hour and writing 12:15.

questions.question: Maya's swim lesson at the Vancouver community pool starts at quarter past 4 in the afternoon. Which digital clock shows the same time as her analog clock at that moment?
questions.explain: Quarter past means the minute hand has gone one quarter of the way around, which is 15 minutes, and the hour hand is only just past the 4, so the digital clock reads 4:15. The trap is letting the hour hand's lean toward the 5 push you to 5:15 — the hour has not changed until the minute hand reaches the 12 again.

questions.question: In the evening Owen's analog clock has the hour hand just past the 6 and the minute hand on the 4. His family's stove uses a 24-hour clock. What does the stove show?
questions.explain: The hour hand is past 6, and the minute hand on the 4 is 4 fives = 20 minutes, so the analog time is 6:20 in the evening; adding 12 for the afternoon gives 18:20. The trap is bumping the hour hand up to the 7 and writing 19:20.

questions.question: An analog clock shows the hour hand just before the 3 and the minute hand on the 10, which is 2:50. What time will it be 10 minutes later?
questions.explain: At 2:50 the minute hand is 10 minutes from the 12, and 50 + 10 = 60 minutes, which is one whole hour, so the clock rolls over to 3:00. The trap is reading the leaning hour hand as 3 already and answering 3:50, or writing 2:60 instead of trading 60 minutes for 1 hour.

questions.question: Liam wants to draw the hands for quarter to 9 on a blank analog clock. Which description of the two hands is correct?
options: The hour hand points right at the 9, and the minute hand points at the 9
The hour hand is a little past the 9, and the minute hand points at the 9
The hour hand is a little before the 9, and the minute hand points at the 3
The hour hand is a little before the 9, and the minute hand points at the 9
questions.explain: Quarter to 9 means 8:45, so the hour is still 8: the hour hand is nearly at the 9 but has not reached it, and the minute hand sits on the 9 for 45 minutes. The trap is putting the hour hand on the 9 or past it, which would say 9:45 instead.

questions.question: Nadia's analog clock has the hour hand very close to the 6 but not quite there, and the minute hand on the 10. Her brother says the time is 6:50. Which answer gives the correct time and the correct reason?
options: 5:50, because the hour hand has not reached the 6 yet
6:50, because the hour hand is almost touching the 6
5:10, because the minute hand is pointing at the number 10
6:10, because the hour is nearly 6 and the minute hand is on the 10
questions.explain: Always name the hour the hour hand has already passed: it is past 5 and not yet 6, so the hour is 5, and the minute hand on the 10 is 10 fives = 50 minutes, giving 5:50. The trap is letting a nearly-there hour hand count as the next hour, which turns 5:50 into 6:50.

questions.question: Soccer practice at Trout Lake Park starts when the analog clock has the hour hand just past the 4 and the minute hand on the 6, in the afternoon. Practice lasts 45 minutes. On the 24-hour clock in the change room, what time does practice end?
questions.explain: The clock reads 4:30 in the afternoon; 30 + 45 = 75 minutes, and 75 minutes is 1 hour and 15 minutes, so practice ends at 5:15 pm, which is 17:15 on a 24-hour clock. The traps are writing 16:75 instead of trading 60 minutes for an hour, and reading the hour hand as one hour too late to get 18:15.

questions.question: Afternoon recess starts at 1:00. Right now the classroom's analog clock has the hour hand a tiny bit past the 12 and the minute hand on the 11. How long until recess starts?
options: Recess has already started, because the clock says 1:55
questions.explain: The hour hand is just past the 12, so the hour is 12, and the minute hand on the 11 is 11 fives = 55 minutes, making it 12:55; from 55 minutes to a full 60 minutes is only 5 more minutes. The trap is reading the hour hand as the 1 and thinking it is 1:55, which makes recess look finished when it has not begun.

questions.question: Ella's piano lesson begins when her analog clock shows the hour hand just past the 6 and the minute hand on the 10. The lesson lasts 30 minutes. She writes the end time as 6:80. What time does the lesson really end?
questions.explain: The clock reads 6:50, and 50 + 30 = 80 minutes; since 60 minutes make 1 hour, trade 60 away to get 1 hour and 20 minutes, so the lesson ends at 7:20. The traps are leaving a minute number bigger than 59, and reading the hour hand as 7 at the start, which pushes the end all the way to 8:20.
